title: HT 86 / HT 95: the strongest audited roster
status: Related records; identity and role unresolved
evidence: Five other labels recur after the Q forms are withheld: DA-ME, DI-DE-RU, KU-NI-SU, MI-NU-TE, SA-RU. The Q entries follow DI-DE-RU in the inspected edition. Two tablets, not four independent witnesses.
test: All five exact-label quantities are 20 on HT86a and 10 on HT95b. Extending that ×2 conversion to the proposed Q pairing predicts 20, but the QA entry is 10. The conjunction of same Q account and universal conversion of equivalent quantities fails.
rival: Spelling variation; distinct related accounts; commodity vocabulary; repeated rosters in separate events. Different grain composites and sections prevent treating a common unit as established.
next: An independent participant/category anchor, followed by a third linked record with an externally recognizable operation. More spelling resemblance is insufficient.
novelty: Roster and Q correspondence are published prior work. Exhaustive ranking and exact conditional scale diagnostic were executed in this iteration; publication priority unestablished.
access: GORILA I pp134–135 and154–155 visually checked.

title: DA-ME / DA-ZA: a misleading database contrast
forms: HT86a DA-ME ↔ frozen SigLA HT95b DA-ZA
evidence: The strongest raw terminal-sign candidate changes when the primary edition is checked. GORILA prints ME in HT95b.2; its damaged-sign apparatus concerns a preceding mark.
test: Keep raw SigLA unchanged; rerun with a named DA-ME reading overlay. The apparent DA-ME/DA-ZA substitution disappears.
rival: A database transcription or interpretation discrepancy, not demonstrated ancient variation. This audit does not diagnose its cause.
next: Retain the discrepancy record; only a documented revised reading should reopen it.
novelty: Source audit and explicit overlay newly executed in this project run.
access: Primary edition normalized table and drawing inspected by root and source researcher.

title: TE-KE / TE-KI, with TE-TU as an explicit rival
forms: HT85a TE-KE ↔ HT122a TE-KI; control HT13 TE-TU
evidence: HT85a and HT122a share DA-RI-DA and the opaque chunk DA-SI-*118 when that chunk is admitted. Published hand attribution puts both under Scribe 9. Broader object overlap adds labels on other faces.
test: HT13 contains TE-KI and TE-TU. Either can be compared to HT85a TE-KE with the same independent companions DA-SI-*118 and KU-*79-NI. Co-occurrence does not itself prove either reading is the same referent.
rival: Short related names or unrelated names; spelling habit; grammar. Similar context does not uniquely select a mapping.
next: An additional identity anchor that chooses TE-KI over TE-TU, and role evidence independent of the last sign.
novelty: TE-KE/TE-KI is published. Explicit rival-context screen newly run; no priority claim.
access: SigLA snapshot; Davis/Valério contextual study. HT13 edition check documented in source note; HT85/122 no fresh full plate audit.

title: HT 117 / HT 87: linked administrative contexts
evidence: Published shared headings/subheadings, DI-KI-SE 1, and attribution to Scribe 9 supply a concrete documentary connection.
test: No independently identified role contrast was recovered. Reading an attendance/absence action depends on contested KI-RO and name classifications.
rival: Related lists, categories or obligations without a written attendance action.
next: Check original plates, then seek a role anchor beyond heading position and KI-RO interpretation.
novelty: Published contextual relationship, retrieved as a control.
access: Primary research article read; original HT87/117 plates not freshly inspected.

title: Seal AT 125 across document types
status: Physical administrative link; no named identity
evidence: Published seal identification connects a roundel and nodules; the publication distinguishes scribal hands.
test: Shared seal identity survives independently of text morphology, but no written designation is independently tied to one historical person or transaction direction.
rival: Institution, office, intermediary, reused instrument, multiple writers.
next: A complete written designation explicitly linked to that seal and an independently known operation.
novelty: Published observation; retrieved control. Older seal142 variant tests are preserved in project history and not counted again.
access: Weingarten article text; no new seal-image comparison.

title: TA-NA family: the earlier target remains blocked
evidence: The expanded search reproduces only the SA-MA bridge when opposite faces of HT10 and ZA10 are aggregated. No local associate packet independently identifies one TA-NA referent.
test: No exclusive initial-A or final-syllable pair with both targets at least three signs has even one independent face associate under the tested complete-chunk screens. This is a bounded indexed-corpus result.
rival: Related designations, distinct entities, site-conditioned spelling, derivation or grammar.
next: A complete physically or transactionally linked witness; do not promote damaged ZA9 or a missing A-TA-NA-TI reconstruction.
novelty: Prior target result confirmed within a broader executed screen.
access: Frozen 802-face snapshot and round9 evidence; no fresh TA-NA autopsy.
